correctness.rationale: For F(x)=x+b-(1+exp(-ax))^(-1), q=exp(-a/6), b=1/3+sigma q, x=-1/2+z/a, the exactly defined scaled 3-step displacement H=q^(-1)(F^3(x)-x) admits uniform C^1 expansion H=3sigma-2sinh(z)+O_S(aq), H_z=-2cosh(z)+O_S(aq), H_sigma=3+O_S(aq) for bounded sigma,z. Its negative derivative, end signs, and implicit differentiation prove the unique local primitive attracting 3-cycle at z=arsinh(3sigma/2)+O_S(aq); multiplier 1-2aq sqrt(1+9sigma^2/4)+O_S(a^2q^2); slope 3/[2aq sqrt(1+9sigma^2/4)](1+O_S(aq)). Verified the derivative identity (mu-1)/(aq)=H_z directly and independently solved exact logistic iterations in high precision for several sigma and a. Tests diagnose, not prove, the all-large-a compact-uniform theorem.
residual_risks: All asymptotics are for bounded sigma and sufficiently large a; local itinerary uniqueness does not imply global attractor uniqueness.
